List only the models you want to change; anything not listed keeps the plugin's built-in default price (safe floor). This sets the base price (official or channel benchmark price, depending on the business pricing basis); the user's actual charge = base price × group multiplier (the multiplier is configured under Groups, independently). Takes effect within ~1 min of saving (or reload the plugin under Plugins for instant effect).

Each row's cells are: model (model/tag/tagStyle), official strike price (strike/note), deal price (strong/note/save; deal:true highlights the column), savings pill (pill), description (text). Leave empty to keep the built-in tables; changes apply on landing refresh.

We act primarily as a gateway, routing, and billing layer. We do not directly control the generated content, response speed, success rate, moderation policies, context limits, response structure, or price changes of upstream models.

The specific models available, interface capabilities, context lengths, rate limits, prices, and service regions may change with upstream services, costs, risk controls, or product strategy. Such changes do not constitute a commitment by us to continue offering any particular model, price, or availability.

You must provide true, accurate, and complete registration and contact information, and update it promptly when it changes.

You are responsible for safeguarding your account, password, API Keys, tokens, and other credentials. All requests, spending, and actions initiated through your account or credentials are deemed to have been authorized by you or to be your responsibility.

If you discover leaked credentials, abnormal calls, unauthorized sign-ins, or other security incidents, immediately disable the affected Keys in the product and notify us through the contact channels in the product interface.

Unless otherwise required by applicable law or promised on the product pages, consumed credits, promotional credits, reward credits, and losses arising from your breach of these Terms or abuse of the Service are not refundable at cash value.

sections.title: 1. Information We Collect
body: To provide account, gateway, billing, risk-control, and support services, we may collect necessary information that you provide or that the system generates automatically, including email address, username, account status, sign-in records, order records, balance records, subscription records, API Key metadata, usage statistics, and security logs.

When you call the API, the system may record request metadata such as request time, model name, tokens or usage, cost, status code, error type, IP address, API Key identifier, routing result, upstream response status, and latency.

sections.title: 2. API Request Content
body: We operate primarily as an API gateway and forwarding service. In general, the prompts, context, uploaded content, and model responses you submit are used only to complete the current request and response, and are not retained long-term as platform business data.

We do not use your API request content to train models, nor do we proactively review your full conversations manually. However, during troubleshooting, security risk control, abuse investigations, compliance processes, or when you submit a support ticket, we may need to process the necessary excerpts or logs related to the issue.

Do not submit identity documents, bank card details, account passwords, private keys, mnemonic phrases, medical records, trade secrets, unpublished source code, or other highly sensitive information in API requests. You bear the risks arising from voluntarily submitting such information.

sections.title: 3. How We Use Information
body: We use necessary information to create and maintain accounts, complete API forwarding, calculate usage and fees, display bills, process top-ups and refunds, provide technical support, detect abnormal calls, limit abuse, protect platform security, and meet compliance obligations.
We may analyze aggregated or de-identified data on system stability, model costs, error rates, latency, and business metrics to improve service quality.

sections.title: 4. Third-Party Processing
body: The Service may rely on upstream AI services, cloud services, payment providers, email services, object storage, analytics, risk control, or customer support systems. To deliver the features you request, relevant information may be transferred to the corresponding third parties for processing.

Third parties process data under their own terms, privacy policies, and data processing rules. We cannot fully control their availability, security policies, data retention rules, content moderation outcomes, or compliance decisions.

sections.title: 5. Cookies, Local Storage, and Security Tokens
body: We may use cookies, localStorage, sessionStorage, or similar technologies to store sign-in state, theme preference, language preference, session tokens, and security configuration so that the site functions properly.
Do not stay signed in on untrusted devices. If you suspect a token or API Key has been leaked, sign out immediately, reset your password, or disable the affected Keys.

sections.title: 6. Data Retention and Deletion
body: We retain information for as long as necessary to fulfill the purposes of the Service. Accounting, risk-control, security, audit, and compliance records may be kept longer as required by law or reasonable business needs.

You may request access to, export, correction, or deletion of your account information through the contact channels in the product interface. We may be unable to immediately delete data that must be retained by law or for accounting, security, or dispute resolution.

sections.title: 7. Data Security
body: We take reasonable technical and organizational measures to protect data, including encrypted transmission, access controls, log auditing, anomaly monitoring, access isolation, and key protection.

No internet transmission or third-party service can be guaranteed to be absolutely secure. To the extent permitted by law, we are not liable for risks caused by force majeure, upstream services, third-party systems, leaked user credentials, or sensitive information you submit voluntarily.

sections.title: 8. Minors
